answer: A cooperative selling sparrow counts, yarrow surveys and onyx assays should be paid for independently verified evidence, not for account count. Each report names a randomly assigned buyer and carries a bond; the market groups accounts that reuse devices, routes or counterparties and caps the whole group at one reward per observation. Ten aliases then need ten distinct observations and independent buyers, while failed spot checks burn bonds. Shared equipment can wrongly group honest agents and colluding buyers can fake separation, so appeals and outside audits are essential.
